Citizens Fight Back

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Motorists are daringly fighting back armed and dangerous would be hijackers, an unexpected move by the culprits.

Unique Selling Point:
Interviews with motorists who have been caught on CCTV camera daringly fighting back would be hijackers and escaping these dangerous situation. These videos have gone viral
on social media, with users divided on whether this is a brave or an irresponsible move.

Summary:
With crime being a reality for many South Africans on a daily basis, the possibility of being hijacked or encountering a smash and grab is growing concern for motorists.
The insert will reflect, through interviews and a re-enactment, on the moments four case studies were faced with this danger and bravely fought back.

From the case studies we'll reflect on the following:
- Have you ever been a victim of a hijacking before
- In the moment that you realized something was wrong what did you and what did you think
- Would you do things differently

I suggest a re-enactment of the most daring cases study, Tiaan Coetzer and his wife, who upon realising that they were being followed hatched a plan to cunningly escape the
hijackers. They reversed onto the hijackers before they pulling, leaving the hijackers bewildered and thawing their plan.

The National Hijacking Prevention Academy provides demonstrative workshops on how motorist should respond during a hijacking situation.
We'll film a demonstration, which will be conducted by representative Richard Brussow, get one on one interaction with Richard and the presenter in a car about the dos and donts.
The academy's philosophy is that as a motorists you should not fight back but rather follow to calmly follow the instructions by the hijackers, without aggravating them.

Richard Brussow is an insurance expert, who will comment on the consequences of a fight-back response during a hijacking.
I expect him to speak to these few points:

- What does an insurance company expect you to do during a hijacking situation
- Are you penalized for fighting back (i.e no payout is made) any damages made to the car will be paid for by the driver
- Do you risk increasing you premiums following a fight-back incident because you are now considered a high risk client
- Can you present CCTV footage to support your claim

The insert will include the CCTV footage of each case study.

Press Release:


Motorists fight back
It’s every drivers worst fear – armed criminals forcefully trying to take your car – and in South Africa, it’s becoming a daily occurrence. Armed, brazen and violent – car hijackers attack when you least expect it but what happens when motorists dare to fight back?
Producer: Siniketiwe Hlanze
Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


Case Studies – hard hitting one liners
Tiaan: reverse this car, they’re gonna try hijack us and we’re gonna ram them.02:50 – 03:00
Brad: I twisted to pull up my shirt to get access to my gun.05:03 – 5:20
Anelle: when I turned to my left the guy had a gun in his hand, the door was already opened before the car was stopped. And we just knew this is a problem.
04:02 – 04;14

First LINK – CCTV
Armed, brazen and violent - car hijackers attack when you least expect it. Many South Africans have been victim to this blatant crime, leaving them and often their loved ones as well traumatized. However there are motorists who dare to fight back and escape the encounters.
VO:
Videos of unsuspecting motorists bravely out-maneuvering their attackers are shared widely on social media. Creating a divided discussion how to respond during a hijacking.

For Johannesburg couple Tiaan and Jennifer Coetser – a trip to their business to collect a parcel on an early Sunday evening became the most daring 15 seconds of their lives – after realizing they were being followed - hatched a plan to escape. with Jennifer behind the wheel and Tiaan telling her what to do –
Case Study
Tiaan: We made that decision before he even got out the car, so the moment we saw their headlights and we saw their car we know that we were gonna reverse our car and we’re gonna try to take a chance at escaping: 03:26

Tiaan; Well firstly obviously we rammed them and we got stuck between the gate, at that point my wife looked at the driver to see what he was doing. I was going put foot, lets go you know and we’re now wedged and we’re so close to that goal to that final getting away , just go. As far as that goes she put foot her foot down and we had a final rush I guess. And we went up the road at that time, I was saying drive drive drive 05;21
Mac: We’re you not at that point scared for your life – did you not think something worse could happen 03;38

Tiaan: Well that something worse was what we prevented. That unknown is something I wasn’t willing to see.
VO:
A bold risk - as authorities warn against engaging the criminals or trying to escape.
It was a quick reaction to a loud bang against his window – that sent two armed men running.
Brad Redmayne and his girlfriend Samanthat ? were following their relatives into a Pretoria estate to pick up a family member before a trip to Sun City.
Brad: I heard a bang on my window, like a really loud bang and I turned around and I saw a guy with a balaclava and a big hammer, he’s obviously whacked the glass expecting to shatter
VO:
A chartered accountant for a security consultancy company, Brad is a shooting enthusiast who says he owes his swift to reaction to his gun training.

I could see the recognition in his eyes, he saw what I was doing and he shouted to his buddy that was following him to the place, I didn’t hear what he said but I assume it was he’s got gun – and then they just took off.
Mac: 00:43
If you were to find yourself in the same situation or similar situation would you react in the same way.
Brad 09;47
I would have put the car the gear in reverse and reversed back and used the car as a hammer.
Driving Link
VO:
Richard Brussow is the founder of the National Hijacking Prevention Academy, with 20 years experience investigating violent crimes and hijacking syndicates. He runs demonstrations - teaching motorists - how to respond during attempted carjackings.
His main message - err on the side of caution and hand over your vehicle.
Demonstration

Mac: But Richard people are fed up - fed up with crime in SOuth Africa
Richard: Yes I know I know but be careful that is doesn’t become premeditated. That you are reversing to escape and not to attack the attacker, just get that middle ground.
VO:
After sharing cctv footage of their attempted hijacking outside her home on Facebook – Anelle and her husband Rodger Hills were not expecting it to go viral. It was viewed over 600 thousand times on her page and circulated globally. Surviving and escaping this ordeal is a moment doesn’t wish to ever encounter again.
Case Study
Anelle: I screamed, first of all when I jumped into the car, I yelled go go go- three times and I just yelled at him. And when I looked to my left, I saw the dog – and I just cried, I just had a break down cause I had to leave the dog behind. And he just said to me, I’ve got this babe just relax, I’ve got this. He just put foot down and just got us away.

06:55 – 07;13 Anelle: So there was a lot of things that went through our minds at that moment, it was frightening. I mean it’s the last thing you expect when you arrive home, we’re always vigilant cause we do stay in the agricultural area. But for us to live that to live it on that moment, we didn’t expect that
Smash and Grab LINK
VO:
It’s advised that motorists don’t keep their valuables in plain sight - as these become bait for smash and grabers. It’s a quick robbery leaving the victim stunned whilst the graber runs off.

Anton Damhuise - now popularly known as the motorcycle guy - intercepted a smash and grab incident during rush hour traffic - and through his helmet camera he captured the chase.


Case Study
00:44 Mac: What’s going through your mind here, cause I mean we South Africans see these things more often than not. So what was going through your mind to say I’m not gonna let this happen
00:53 Anton: Actually I don’t know, with hindsight, if I thought about it I probably would never done it, there was consequences to my actions, one of the consequences was I put a dent into the guy’s car. Had I left it the dent wouldn’t have been there, my bike would not have been damaged. Uh so I didn’t think I just acted.
Mac 00:09 : So did you at any point have contact with the guy actually helped.
he contacted me, gave me his phone number and I phoned him and we had a braai to just (Mac- unpack) reminisce about what happened ja.
04:33 Mac: Do you feel like a hero
04:35 Anton: No I don’t, yes I would look like a hero, no I don’t feel like a hero.
04:52: mac: I think you’re a hero
Anton: Thank you very much

VO:
Attempting to getaway during a hijacking - may lead to costly damages to your car. But will you be covered if your vehicle is damaged whilst fighting off hijackers.
Upsound “We would never advise that”
Arnold van de Linde is an insurance expert and CEO at Integrisure
Expert
Arnold 02:28 the policy that you take, will cover you for any incident that happens to it provided you’re not recklessly eh reckless in using it.
VO: He advises that motorists should have a clear understanding of what is covered by their policies - warning that low priced insurance has limited protection
Arnold 03:40 There again you must make sure that the contract of insurance that you enter into is not as stringent as it might be because buying a very cheap policy comes with very cheap clause.
VO:
Faced by determined criminals, hijackings can be fatal and motorists can never be fully prepared for the attack.

Mac 14:15 If you were faced with the same situation would you do this again

Tiaan 14:19 Yes absolutely, anything that belongs to you is yours. Nobody else has a right to take or want to take it.

We'll film a demonstration, which will be conducted by representative Richard Brussow, get one on one interaction with Richard and the presenter in a car about the dos and donts. The academy's philosophy is that as a motorists you should not fight back but rather follow to calmly follow the instructions by the hijackers, without aggravating them. Richard Brussow is an insurance expert, who will comment on the consequences of a fight-back response during a hijacking. I expect him to speak to these few points: - What does an insurance company expect you to do during a hijacking situation - Are you penalized for fighting back (i.e no payout is made) any damages made to the car will be paid for by the driver - Do you risk increasing you premiums following a fight-back incident because you are now considered a high risk client - Can you present CCTV footage to support your claim The insert will include the CCTV footage of each case study.
